meaning.observed: Direct evidence for the named operation in the stated profile and build. Guest playback or guest Maps navigation does not establish signed-in behavior.
meaning.partial: One or more relevant steps ran. The intended result or a necessary control remains unverified.
meaning.open: The records cited for the app do not demonstrate the named operation.

sign_in.evidence: The original app reached its signed-in screen from a fresh app profile.  Re-observed 2026-11-19 on the rebuilt dedicated host (user-approved install; uid unchanged): Sign in with Google opened Play services' account chooser, the account choice returned RESULT_OK, and FotMob showed its signed-in account.

private_preference_cloud_round_trip.evidence: The changed favorite was restored after the local favorites cache was cleared. The read endpoint also accepted an invalid-token control, so the read alone does not establish authorization. Re-observed 2026-11-19: a team followed while signed in; FotMob stopped and its four local favorite-team files moved aside; after restart FotMob re-created them, including the sync ETag file, and showed all three teams. The added team was then removed again.

silent_token_renewal.evidence: A fresh signed ID token reached FotMob after expiry of its saved token. Re-observed 2026-11-19 on the rebuilt host: FotMob's last ID tokens were issued at 09:30 PST; after a restart at 12:35 PST Play services issued FotMob's ID token again without any screen, three hours later and past the token's one-hour lifetime, and FotMob stayed signed in.

restart_persistence.evidence: The signed-in UI and account identifier survived client restart. Re-observed 2026-11-19: after a full restart FotMob opened signed in.

sign_in.evidence: With the user's approval and test sign-up details, Google sign-in from Spotify's Create account returned RESULT_OK (account chooser offered the account) and Spotify created its account; the signed-in home showed the account avatar.

account_session.evidence: The signed-in home and Your Library belonged to the new account (avatar, followed artists from onboarding).

library_load.evidence: Your Library loaded the account's followed artists from the server.

playback.evidence: An artist's play button started a track: pause control, equalizer mark and mini-player shown, and the progress bar advanced between captures; playback was then paused. Physical audibility was not measured.

silent_token_renewal.gap: While signed in, Spotify made no Google token request at any later start, including starts after the token's one-hour lifetime. Its Log out also signs it out of Google: Log in with Google then showed Google's account chooser (an interactive choice, not a silent renewal); choosing the account signed it back in. The app gives no path on which a silent renewal can be observed. Spotify made no silent token request at sign-up either.

restart_persistence.evidence: After a full restart of the Spotify process, the app opened signed in with the last track restored in the mini-player.

sign_in.evidence: Sign up with Google returned RESULT_OK; with the user's approval and test details Wattpad created the account and opened its signed-in home.

account_session.evidence: The profile page showed the new account (display name from Google, username, joined minutes earlier).

library_or_reading.evidence: A public classic opened in the reader with its first chapter rendered. (A story added during onboarding did not appear in the Library tab.)

silent_token_renewal.evidence: While signed in, Wattpad made no Google token request at any later start, including starts after the token's one-hour lifetime. Its Log out also signs it out of Google: Log in with Google then showed Google's account chooser (an interactive choice, not a silent renewal); choosing the account signed it back in. The app gives no path on which a silent renewal can be observed. (Earlier: expiry of the local SDK selection led back to signup.) Its one silent token request followed the account choice.

restart_persistence.evidence: After a full restart of the Wattpad process, the app opened signed in (a Premium offer, closed, then the signed-in home).

sign_in.evidence: With the delegated broker grant (eight scopes taken from YouTube's own code, 24-hour native consent) and the silent-token fix for the notification flag, the original app listed the account with its YouTube identity and signed in; the signed-in Subscriptions page showed the account avatar.

account_session.evidence: The account tab showed the account's own page, including its private Watch later and Liked videos lists.

video_playback.evidence: The original APK played a public clip to the end. Repeats included a retained guest profile. Signed-in playback and physical audibility remain open. 2026-11-18, signed in, current build: pre-roll ads played with advancing frames; the chosen public video showed its first frame and then stopped advancing for over a minute. The app's own UI below and over the video stayed black: the video's surface window sits above the app's window (known order gap), so its controls were not visible. Signed-in playback remains open. 2026-11-19 with the window content fix (signed in): the watch page kept its title, buttons, comments and next video drawn below the playing video; frames advanced for about 30 seconds, then the player reported a playback problem, and a retry stopped at the same position. OpenHarmony's video decoder logged no error. Signed-in playback to the end remains open. 2026-11-19, three signed-in playback sessions of the same public video: each played 25 to 45 seconds of new video and then reported a playback problem, starting at 0:00, 0:34 and 0:56, at 480p and with 360p chosen in the player. YouTube used its own bundled native Cronet; the only failing socket calls were IPv6 connects on the IPv4-only network and a missing local socket. Cause not established: a stream limit the server applies (for example to a session it does not trust) and a fault in later media requests both remain possible. The guest comparison could not run: YouTube's account popup did not take taps.

restart_persistence.evidence: After a full restart of the YouTube process, the app came back signed in: signed-in Subscriptions page and account avatar. Re-observed 2026-11-18: after a full restart YouTube opened signed in.

account_selection.evidence: On the fresh dedicated host (its own host and initially empty app data), Gmail's setup listed the test account and Take me to Gmail entered that account's mailbox. Sync first had to be turned on in Gmail's account settings; with the Google-account sync default (local 13b664f) and no explicit setting, the same host synced by itself at start and showed no sync-off notice.

mailbox_sync.evidence: In the earlier delegated configuration, original Gmail populated its inbox and opened an existing message after enabling sync and restarting. Re-observed 2026-11-18: after its host was killed and the launch restarted, original Gmail synced and showed the inbox with the account's mail.

refresh.evidence: A message the user sent at 18:49 PST was not in the original Gmail's inbox at 18:55; a manual pull at 18:55:40 showed it at the top within 15 seconds (no sync-adapter job ran, so Gmail's pull uses its own fetch). Earlier, after the network compat library fix, Gmail's automatic sync after start had fetched the first test message.

restart_persistence.evidence: The earlier configuration retained the account, inbox and automatic-sync preference across a client restart. The dedicated fresh-profile control stopped at setup. After the account provider was restored, it verified a newly restarted original Gmail process and the retained Primary inbox reappeared. Re-observed 2026-11-18: the same relaunch opened signed in without any account step.

account_selection.evidence: On the current build, a fresh dedicated Drive (its own host, its retained app data moved aside, an empty data directory) listed the device's Google account through the account service, received tokens through official Play services, and opened that account's Drive with its files; it made no add-account request. With one Google account on the device Drive selected it without asking; its account menu showed that account under Switch account with no other to choose. The menu greeted 'Hi there!' without the profile name.

file_listing.evidence: My Drive listed the approved fixture after a process restart. The current account-path retest did not reach the file list. Re-observed 2026-11-18 on the current build: a fresh dedicated Drive listed the account's files, and listed them again after a full restart.

file_open.evidence: The original Drive preview rendered the three expected lines of the 107-byte file. The current account-path retest did not reach the file list. Re-observed 2026-11-18 on the current build: the validation fixture opened and its text rendered, with tokens through official Play services.

token_renewal.evidence: In one running Drive process, the last token was issued at 17:15:42 PST. Opening the fixture at 18:29:06, 73 minutes later and past the one-hour token lifetime, made Play services accept a silent request; the broker issued a new token under the native consent, and the fixture content rendered.

restart_persistence.evidence: The same profile listed and opened the fixture after restart. Its contents could have been cached. The current account-path retest did not reach the file list. Re-observed 2026-11-18: after a full restart Drive opened signed in with its files listed.

startup.evidence: Original Maps opened in guest mode. Re-observed 2026-11-18 on the current build: original Maps opened in guest mode.

map_tiles.evidence: The guest UI displayed labeled map tiles. Re-observed 2026-11-18: labeled map tiles rendered, and street-level tiles after search.

search.evidence: Guest place search returned a result with the services connected. Signed-in place search remains open. Re-observed 2026-11-18 (guest): the same place query moved the map to the result and placed a pin. After the keyboard opened, Maps' own controls and place card stayed hidden under the map surface (window order gap); the query was typed through the test input path. Re-observed 2026-11-19 with the window content fix (westlake 6b80c26, guest): after the search the map moved to the place and its place card (Directions, Share, Save, photos) stayed on screen over the map.

real_location.evidence: OpenHarmony accepted two requests during the temporary permission grant. No real fix was delivered. Permission was restored to Deny. With GNSS disabled, the adapter now reports GPS disabled to Android and withholds explicit GPS requests. Original Maps exercised the change on its dedicated host. Network provider configuration and a physical fix remain open. A board fixture verified provider selection, source filtering and per-provider caches on the rebuilt adapter. Original Maps queried last location with its host permission denied. It received zero physical fixes.

route_preview.evidence: The guest directions screen displayed a route preview between specified endpoints. 2026-11-18: not re-observed. From the start screen the directions button did not open the directions screen; after a search, Maps' controls stayed hidden under the map surface. The earlier observation stands. Re-observed 2026-11-19 with the window content fix (guest): from the place card, Directions, a start point typed and chosen from the suggestions; Maps drew both endpoints, the route lines and its route sheet (driving time and distance, transit and walking times, Preview).

restart_persistence.evidence: The retained guest configuration survived restart and repeated the directions flow. Re-observed 2026-11-18: after a full restart guest Maps opened with tiles and its controls.

sign_in.evidence: On the earlier shared host, Google accepted basic profile and email consent in web sign-in, then Uber displayed “Sorry, we could not find that page”. On the current dedicated host the signed rider app displayed its welcome page. The trip-link window disappeared before a Google tap, and the normal launch displayed the Uber logo before the board returned to Gmail. Rider sign-in remains partial.

account_session.gap: No authenticated rider session was observed.

destination_search.gap: Uber opened onboarding for a link with fixed endpoints. The user did not exercise in-app destination search.

restart_persistence.gap: No authenticated rider session was available for a restart test.

sign_in.evidence: Facebook login completed in the original FotMob flow. On the fresh dedicated host the Facebook form appeared. That separate run did not complete authentication. Its SDK form remained visible after Back in Spotify.

authenticated_return.evidence: The SDK returned to the original FotMob app. An independent check of the Facebook account endpoint matched the app-saved identity.

account_session.evidence: The account menu showed the signed-in session.

restart_persistence.evidence: The account and signed-in UI survived process restart.

sign_in.evidence: Facebook accepted login and showed its consent screen.

authenticated_return.evidence: The Facebook SDK and original Wattpad onboarding activity received a successful result.

account_session.evidence: Observed 2026-11-19 on the D600 (same delegated configuration). The dedicated Wattpad's Facebook web login, with the user's test login typed through a masked helper, again reached Facebook's reCAPTCHA; the user completed it on the board (the agent does not solve CAPTCHAs). The 11-18 attempt had stopped there. Facebook then returned to Wattpad, which opened its own "Create an Account" form; a new Facebook-linked Wattpad account was created with the test defaults (no marketing). Wattpad's home and profile showed the account with the Facebook profile's name and picture and a Facebook link.

restart_persistence.evidence: Observed 2026-11-19: Wattpad was stopped and started again (a new app process). It reopened on its home signed in, and its profile showed the same Facebook-linked account.

sign_in.evidence: Observed 2026-11-19 on the D600 (same delegated configuration). Spotify's Facebook login opened Facebook's web form inside Spotify. The user's test login was typed through a masked helper; Facebook answered with its reCAPTCHA, which the user completed on the board (the agent does not solve CAPTCHAs). Facebook then signed in and granted the requested scopes. Earlier records showed the empty form only.

authenticated_return.evidence: Observed 2026-11-19: Facebook's redirect back to Spotify reached Spotify's Facebook callback activity, which Westlake launched in Spotify's own process, and the result was delivered to Facebook's login activity. Spotify then handled the login itself: it answered "Signing up with Facebook isn't available right now. Try signing up with your email." and opened its email sign-up. Codex's earlier run had stopped before any return.

account_session.gap: Not observable with this Facebook account: after the authenticated return, Spotify's own service refused to create an account through Facebook ("Signing up with Facebook isn't available right now"), and the test Facebook account has no Spotify account. Observing it needs a Spotify account already linked to this Facebook account, or a user-approved scope change. Spotify was signed back in with Google afterwards.

restart_persistence.gap: Not observable with this Facebook account: after the authenticated return, Spotify's own service refused to create an account through Facebook ("Signing up with Facebook isn't available right now"), and the test Facebook account has no Spotify account. Observing it needs a Spotify account already linked to this Facebook account, or a user-approved scope change. Spotify was signed back in with Google afterwards.
